recipes.name: Alex's Raw Chocolate Pudding
ingredients_raw: 1 avocado - peeled, pitted, and cut into chunks
1 banana, peeled and cut into chunks

steps.text: Place avocado, banana, soy milk, cocoa powder, agave nectar, lemon juice, and coconut into a blender. Cover, and puree until smooth. Divide into small containers, and store in the refrigerator 1 hour until set.

raw_recipe.headline: Alex's Raw Chocolate Pudding
raw_recipe.description: This recipe is made with all raw ingredients. The combination of avocado, banana, and raw cocoa nibs may seem odd, but the banana provides the taste, and the avocado adds texture, and the cocoa nibs add crunch.
raw_recipe.name: Alex's Raw Chocolate Pudding

review.reviewBody:
Awesome recipe, Alex! I just happened to have a banana and an avacado that needed to get used so I whipped this up and yum! Subbed honey for the agave and added a little vanilla but that's it. I will be making this again for sure. Have been making this about twice a week and have found that adding a tablespoon or 2 of peanut butter makes it like a PB cup pudding. Yum! *******UPDATE***** I added a little extra soy milk and ran it through my ice cream machine with great results. Kind of like a Frosty but nicer. Also makes killer pudding pops. Sometimes I add granola to the pudding for breakfast, too. I love this recipe.
*new update*
Didn't have a banana so I used just the avocado, honey, some nestle's quick (it's what I had), and milk. Better than anything out of a plastic cup. Yum. Next time I'm adding some malt. Thanks, Alex. This is one of the best recipes ever.

This is not just a healthy recipe pretending to taste good. It is actually good. I used almond milk and half dutch cocoa and half chocolate nibs for the chocolate. Put it in my NutriBullet and it was ready in seconds. Will definitely make again.

There are some amazingly talented "health" food geniuses out there! This tasted a lot like chocolate pudding. it had the right texture too. It all blended up so quick and smooth in my Vitamix mixer. The only change I made was using unsweetened almond milk instead of soy and using a frozen sliced banana. I highly suggest using a frozen banana. The pudding will be nice and cold and perfectly thickened as pudding should be. I would also definitely stick with the agave. It is sweeter than honey and it doesn't have any real specific flavor. Thanks, this will come in handy for a sweet but healthier way to satisfy a craving.

I just made it, it's setting in the fridge, I licked the bowl - absolutely added some around 2 Tbs raw peanut butter and a dash of vanilla. I'm so excited!!! It won't need so long to set as it's already creamy. Oh right, I used coconut milk as well...and some maple and honey instead of agave. Whatever, it's amazing and I'm psyched to eat something healthy that is so yummy!

This is very good. I used a frozen banana and a small avocado. Did not have agave nectar so used what was on hand: honey. Also, only had vanilla soy milk, so used that as well. Lastly, only had sweetened coconut flakes. Regardless, this recipe was excellent. You would never know it was made with an avocado but there is a definite banana taste. Also, had some almond milk on hand and used 1/4 cup.

I am the original submitter of this recipe and am so pleased with how many people have enjoyed this. Thanks for the feedback (good or bad)!!! I finally got to try this on some other family members when they came to stay with us for a few days. They were all looking at me like I was crazy, but everyone tried it. Three out of four were really impressed and two asked for seconds. My younger brother said it tasted too much like the cocao. Oh well, you can't please them all! :) Based on one of the other reviewers, I made frozen chocolate pops with the pudding by simply pooring the mixture into ice cube trays and sticking a toothpick in each cube. It was a stifling 108 degrees outside today here in the Arizona desert and these little treats certainly made it easier to get through the hot afternoon!

Update 1/19/12 -- i have been making this fir such a long time and i have my own variation now thta i thinks beats the original. Use one large very ripe avocado, and one barely ripe banana. Note the distinction! Omit the coconut completely. Substitute 1/4 c honey for the agave. Substitute 1 cup vanilla coconut milk for the soy milk. Add 1/2 tsp vanilla extract. You wont be sorry!!!!

5 stars for the sheer genius of this recipe! It's healthy and tasty - a true guilt free dessert. A couple things to mention - this is best served very cold. Otherwise the avocado taste comes through a little. Also, if you don't like banana, you may not care for this. The banana flavor is unmistakable. In fact this really should be called chocolate-banana pudding. But really, there are no complaints from me. I liked my bowl clean :)

I just made this recipe tonight. It is delicious! It is amazing that by using an avocado and banana and using no processed sugar, just natural, you can come up with a chocolate pudding. I will enjoy this so much more knowing that it is healthy! I didn't put the coconut in the recipe and I did use unsweetened almond milk. I may toast some coconut and put it on top when I have more!

AMAZING! I was super skeptical, but man this was awesome! Have to let it chill completely to pull it off, though. I took others advice and added 1/2 tsp vanilla. Tricked my 4 year old into thinking it was her sweet treat for the day so I have no complaints...except it was hard to get her to share it! I loved it. Could serve at a kids party as pudding parfaits and noone would ever know. Stellar job.

The taste just like chocolate pudding! I get my chocolate fix and some good or me nutrients - so I don't feel (too) guilty. I froze my pudding to satisfy my other guilty pleasure ice cream! I will make again for sure .

this recipe was amazing! such a tasty and healthy treat. i used unsweetened almond milk instead of soy milk, honey instead of agave nectar, 2 tablespoons of shredded coconut, and added 1/4 teaspoon of cinnamon.
Surprisingly decadent! Made as written, but did not opt for coconut. Perfect dessert or snack!
So delicious and hard to believe it has no sugar - we loved it! Thanks for sharing such a great recipe.
It was good, healthy and I'll make it again.
doesnt even need sweetner when i used frozen ripe bananas!
Had an odd taste. Not sure if it was the avocado or bitterness of coco.
This is pretty gross! I added some brown sugar and it was 'better'. How this is classed as 'amazing' is beyond me!
I liked how simple it was to make. I regret having added coconut flakes. I don't think they go well with the pudding. My boyfriend described the flavor as "vegetably", but I liked it.
Very good. Tastes more like banana than chocolate, but it is good.

I made this for healthy breakfasts. I did use the unsweetened coconut, which did give it a nice texture with it was shredded up by the blender. I garnished with some semi-sweet chocolate chips and kiwi slices. It could have been sweeter (and I don't like sweets), but I think it is because I used honey instead of agave nectar. Also, I used 2 avocados because the ones I bought were small and I ended up with 4 pretty large servings. Bonus: super easy
